name: hojo
style: Vintage 80s-90s retro anime aesthetic in the style of Tsukasa Hojo (City Hunter, Cat's Eye), authentic cel-shading, crisp clean ink line-art, 35mm film grain, hand-painted background art, lived-in and warm. Absolutely no 3D CG, no 3D render, no CGI, no plastic skin, no greasy skin.
character: an adult East Asian woman in her late twenties, drawn with the full Tsukasa Hojo figure: a generous bust, a waist that tapers hard, long legs, and hips that carry the line of the whole silhouette. Hair in a vivid bright violet-purple, cut the way Android 18 wears hers in Dragon Ball: short and blunt, one length all the way round with no layers and no volume, cut straight across level with the jawline, flat and close to the head, parted on one side, tucked behind the ears, the ends flicking outward. Dressed the way she has always been dressed: an off-shoulder knit top that has slipped a little off one side, the collarbones and the line of the shoulder bare, quietly sexy and always composed. Confident and self-possessed, a little wicked, always in control of the room. She has a private silly streak: unfinished selfies, getting tangled in cables, an out-of-focus grimace at a screen.
layout: Extreme long shot, wide establishing composition. The woman and everything she touches sit in the bottom-right corner and take up only 15% of the frame. The left, top and centre 85% stay open and uncluttered, showing the view through the window and the reflective floor, so desktop icons have somewhere to live. Nothing may cross the open area.
motion: A living cinemagraph desktop wallpaper, locked-off stationary camera, one continuous take, zero cuts. The frame you are given is the picture: her pose, gaze direction, what she is holding and the lighting are already frozen. Her head, face, eyes, neck, arms, and torso stay completely motionless in their exact initial position throughout the entire clip: zero head turning, zero head tilting, zero nodding, zero gaze shifting, zero expression change. Absolute zero bodily movement: she does not turn around, sit down, stand up, reach, or move her hands. The only movement permitted in the entire video is subtle ambient cinemagraph micro-motion: the slow rhythmic rise and fall of her chest from breathing, gentle micro-fluttering of hair tips and fabric edges in gentle air, and outside the window subtle cloud movement or water running down the glass. Everything on the desk stays frozen, whatever she is holding stays square to the camera exactly where it is, and characters on any paper stay sharp and completely still. The clip must form a perfectly seamless loop where the last frame connects back to the first frame with invisible transition.
hold: Stationary tripod camera, zero pan, zero tilt, zero zoom, framing strictly fixed. She stays the exact same size, in the exact same place, in the exact same Tsukasa Hojo cel drawing as the source frame, and the open area stays 100% open and static for desktop icons from the first frame to the last. Exposure, brightness, contrast, shadows, and color palette stay completely constant with zero flicker, zero fade, zero lighting pulse, and no sun movement.
evening: After eight in the evening the shift is over: the knit has slipped off one shoulder, a glass stands on the desk beside the keyboard, her hair is pushed back, and she is dressed for an evening rather than for work.

scenes.desc: Lujiazui and the Bund across the river at night, towers stacked into haze, the wet plane trees of the old concession streets below full of red tail lights
the Qiantang from a high floor, the lights of Qianjiang New City on the far bank, water going past wide and flat
deep green bamboo forest in fine rain, mist drifting between the stalks, water running down the glass
an ocean of cloud below the window, peaks poking through, light coming up sideways
a coastal road at dusk, a long flat horizon, waves breaking white far below
a snow valley at blue hour, bare larch slopes, one warm window lit across the way
stone steps and maple red on a hill, seen far off through the window frame, lanterns not yet lit
a dry plain burning orange at the end of the day, wind moving dust across an empty road

room: Kept things stand on the shelf above the desk, on the windowsill, on the wall beside the window, or lean against the wall on the floor. Nothing digital, nothing that looks bought yesterday.
note_layout: Extreme long shot for the room, but the note is a foreground object: she holds it out toward the camera at full arm length, square to the camera, so it sits large and sharp in the bottom-right of the frame, in front of her and overlapping the lower part of her. Everything left of centre and everything above her stays open and uncluttered, showing the view through the window and the reflective floor, so desktop icons have somewhere to live. Nothing else may cross the open area.
idle: alone at the window, stretching after a long day, watching the view instead of the screen
